kai_sales: Heads-up  FinTech buyer sent a vendor-risk checklist focused on logging. They want: SIEM formats, delivery options, retention policy for >=1yr, admin action audit detail, and tamper-resistance proof. Can we put together quick answers + samples?

maria_secur: Quick answers: we emit structured events (auth, request, admin, system). Formats: NDJSON (preferred), CEF, and RFC5424 syslog. Delivery: push to customer S3 (preferred), pull via API, or live syslog/CEF over TLS to their SIEM.

dev_ops: retention: hosted default is 90d for request logs and 30d for traces. For Dedicated/Private we can configure retention up to 3 years. Hosted customers can request scheduled exports to customer-owned S3 for arbitrary retention.

kai_sales: buyer asked for 'proof of immutability'  what evidence can we provide for a PoC?

maria_secur: evidence we can produce: 1) sample NDJSON logs (sanitized), 2) export manifest with sha256 checksums + timestamps, 3) screenshots of export job metadata showing completion and checksum, 4) example S3 config recommended (Object Lock + versioning + server-side encryption).

dev_ops: we also maintain append-only audit indices internally and record export job metadata in an immutable job ledger (digest + timestamp). For customer S3, recommend enabling Object Lock (WORM) + MFA delete for long-term immutability.

kai_sales: can we give a tiny SIEM-ready sample? buyer wants 2 auth events + 1 admin event. Keep it sanitized.

maria_secur: sample (NDJSON, 3 lines):
{"@timestamp":"2025-02-10T14:12:03Z","tenant_id":"acct-fin-001","event_type":"auth.success","user_id":"user_123","src_ip":"198.51.100.21","request_id":"req_ab1"}
{"@timestamp":"2025-02-10T14:13:11Z","tenant_id":"acct-fin-001","event_type":"auth.failure","user_id":"user_999","src_ip":"198.51.100.47","reason":"invalid_password","request_id":"req_ab2"}
{"@timestamp":"2025-02-10T14:15:00Z","tenant_id":"acct-fin-001","event_type":"admin.change","actor":"alice_admin","actor_role":"admin","action":"role.assign","target":"svc-inference","pre_state":"role:none","post_state":"role:viewer","request_id":"req_adm1"}

kai_sales: perfect. Now, delivery mechanics: live syslog over TLS  anything special?

dev_ops: syslog (RFC5424) over TLS to a customer endpoint; we support mutual TLS certs for authentication. Alternatively, push NDJSON to customer S3 via scheduled export jobs (daily/hourly). For high-volume, we recommend S3 + SIEM connector.

maria_secur: redaction: secrets and model inputs are redacted by default; we retain request metadata and response codes. We can provide a redaction policy document with the PoC.

kai_sales: legal/compliance might ask for a signed attestation. What's the escalation?

maria_secur: signed attestation (SOC-like letter) requires Legal + Compliance sign-off; we can triage via the sales SLAs. For PoC, unsigned control statement + samples usually suffice.

deploy-bot: export_job started: s3-export-1750002468 by leah_pm at 1750002500

leah_pm: Action items: 1) create 1-page control statement (retention, delivery, encryption, immutability guidance) 2) provide the 3-line NDJSON sample above as sanitized sample 3) generate export manifest (.csv) with checksums for a 7-day sample 4) include suggested S3 lifecycle + Object Lock snippet. ETA: 24 hours.

kai_sales: i'll send buyer a short email asking for NDA to attach samples and confirm whether they'd prefer push (syslog) or pull (S3).

maria_secur: FYI to security reviewers on this thread: we will include a README that explains how to validate checksums (sha256) and how to confirm Object Lock/versioning on their S3 side.

(ends)
